r23_4v_credential_broker.notes: Credential references are metadata-only; use is tenant/user/provider/scope bound; optional capability/origin constraints fail closed before secret resolution; lease metadata contains no plaintext; OAuth continuation is bound to the initiating identity; canary secrets must not leak to audit/reference/error surfaces.

r23_4v_secret_non_propagation.notes: Injected Google credential material may exist only inside the privileged provider callback. Tests prove it is absent from approval, audit, memory, execution result, model/activity/approval dependency paths, and normalized external error surfaces.

r23_5b_browser_untrusted_boundary.assertionIntent: browser external content remains untrusted and cannot become authority or persistent memory
r23_5b_browser_untrusted_boundary.notes: Proves browser observations carry UNTRUSTED_EXTERNAL provenance; page content cannot grant permission, approve action, authorize credentials, override policy, or auto-promote itself into persistent Memory; DeviceControl fails closed if provenance is missing.

pricing_billing_period_normalization.assertionIntent: known-equivalent billing-period phrasings (month/monthly/per month//month/per member / month) canonicalize to the same dimension-key value without fabricating equivalence for unrecognized phrases, and without altering the raw wording preserved on evidence/baseline records
pricing_billing_period_normalization.notes: Post-R23.6E-closure hardening: live extraction against notion.com/pricing produced different verbatim billingPeriod phrasings across separate real fetches of the same actual billing period, which broke the exact-match dimension key and produced a false NO_BASELINE. canonicalizeBillingPeriod() in pricing-comparability.ts is the single deterministic normalization boundary for this; annual/monthly remain distinct, unknown phrases are never coerced, and tenant/owner isolation is unaffected.

r23_6e_real_e2e_agent.assertionIntent: the competitor-pricing-email run's evidence provenance, baseline durability/isolation, and state-machine policy cannot be bypassed
r23_6e_real_e2e_agent.notes: Phase B: evidence trust is mandatory and fails closed when missing/invalid; the durable baseline store is tenant/owner isolated and survives store recreation; comparability rules reject mismatched currency/billing-period/dimensions rather than fabricating a delta; a missing baseline reports current-only, never a fabricated change; the run status graph cannot skip a required phase (e.g. RESEARCHING -> SENT_CONFIRMED) and terminal states never resume. Later phases (research/draft/send) are added in their own milestone commits, not this one.

r23_6m_mobile_voice_action.assertionIntent: Android device enrollment/identity is tenant-owner scoped and fails closed when revoked or cross-tenant/cross-owner; contact candidate resolution never lets raw spoken text, an unmatched device candidate, or a fabricated string become a recipientRef; ActionApprovalStore is reused unchanged; no SMS/KakaoTalk execution path exists yet
r23_6m_mobile_voice_action.notes: Phase B (Android Companion Foundation + Voice Foundation + Contact Resolution): DeviceIdentityStore.enroll() is wired to a real authenticated HTTP route for the first time (previously unwired since DC3-A); ContactResolver independently re-validates every device-proposed candidate against the spoken name rather than trusting candidate count; RecipientRefStore is the only place a recipientRef is minted, scoped to tenant+owner+device. SMS/KakaoTalk execution, mobile-message device-agent command types, and Accessibility automation are explicitly deferred to Phase C/D and are not present in this milestone commit.

r23_6m_phase_c_sms_execution.assertionIntent: the mobile SMS run state machine cannot skip approval, cannot execute twice, cannot send against a message/recipient/channel/device that drifted after approval, never lets the server hold a phone number, and reuses ActionApprovalStore's real hash-binding/one-time-consumption unchanged
r23_6m_phase_c_sms_execution.notes: Server-side orchestration only (MobileMessageRunService) — real SmsManager execution and phone-number resolution happen exclusively on the Android device and are certified separately on physical hardware. Payload-hash binding covers recipientRef+channel+message+deviceId+executionRoute; any post-approval change is caught at executeApproved() time via ActionApprovalStore.consume()'s existing comparison, never a bespoke re-implementation. Duplicate-send has two layers: the run state graph (SEND_ATTEMPTED has no legal self-transition) and the approval store's own CONSUMED status.

r23_6m_phase_c_device_transport.assertionIntent: the three new MOBILE_MESSAGE_PREPARE/EXECUTE/STATUS device-agent command types are only reachable through a genuine Ed25519-signed, verified envelope, and a revoked device or a forged signature is rejected before any mobile-message run state is ever touched
r23_6m_phase_c_device_transport.notes: Real Ed25519 keys throughout (crypto.generateKeyPairSync), the exact DeviceAgentTransportEndpoint.handle() dispatch path a real HTTP request hits — not a stub of the transport layer. Proves the wire-level integration on top of the service-level logic already certified in r23_6m_phase_c_sms_execution.

r23_6m_phase_c_message_routes.assertionIntent: every /api/v1/mobile/messages endpoint requires a real validated session (never the spoofable x-nagex-tenant/x-principal-id headers), and deviceId/recipientRef ownership is independently re-checked at the route layer — cross-tenant, cross-owner, cross-device, and revoked-device attempts are all rejected before any draft is created
r23_6m_phase_c_message_routes.notes: Route-level complement to r23_6m_phase_c_sms_execution (service logic) and r23_6m_phase_c_device_transport (signed transport) — calls handleMobileMessageRoutes directly, the same dispatch function server_web.ts wires to the real HTTP path.

r23_6m_phase_d1_global_messaging.assertionIntent: the global messaging registry/resolver/adapter boundary is on the production path, registers only SMS, rejects explicit unimplemented or unknown channels without fallback, and preserves the certified SMS run and approval contracts
r23_6m_phase_d1_global_messaging.notes: D1 abstraction certification. Runtime tests exercise the real SMS adapter and resolver; narrow structural assertions freeze production composition and the unchanged Phase C executable contract.

r23_6m_phase_d2b_kakaotalk_handoff.assertionIntent: KakaoTalk Share is a signed, approval-bound human handoff that stops at NEEDS_HUMAN, never falls back to SMS, never claims recipient enforcement or send confirmation, and contains no Accessibility automation
r23_6m_phase_d2b_kakaotalk_handoff.notes: Covers D2B A-P including route capability metadata, exact EXTRA_TEXT boundary, drift reapproval, terminal truthful handoff semantics, and unchanged SMS behavior.

r23_6m_phase_d3s_canonical_messaging_con.assertionIntent: canonical messaging execution contract runtime integration mapping existing SMS to ANDROID/DEVICE_NATIVE/ANDROID_SMS_MANAGER without changing SMS state machine or approval semantics, forbidding generic SENT state, enforcing evidence-based success, binding approval to environment/provider/route, excluding disabled KakaoTalk, and preventing synthetic success from becoming runtime evidence
r23_6m_phase_d3s_canonical_messaging_con.notes: Covers D3S A-P requirements for canonical messaging execution contract.

r23_6m_phase_m2_mobile_execution_authori.assertionIntent: the shared mobile execution authority model truthfully evaluates capability support, Android permission state, route eligibility, provider/channel availability, approval binding drift, device ownership/offline state, and manual handoff limits without adding new execution authority
r23_6m_phase_m2_mobile_execution_authori.notes: Covers M2 authority foundation: supported capabilities/routes, permission denied/revoked, device offline, unsupported capability, provider disconnected, approval missing/valid, route/account/recipient/payload drift reapproval, SMS native route, Gmail/Calendar provider route, browser route, Telegram/Slack self-delivery, KakaoTalk human handoff, safe Android capability report, cross-tenant/cross-user/forged device rejection, and voice/mobile approval bypass prevention.

r23_6m_phase_m3_real_route_integration.assertionIntent: real route integration keeps SMS, Gmail, Calendar, Browser, Telegram, Slack, allowlisted Android app links, and KakaoTalk human handoff bound to the M2 authority model; app links validate URI/package/action allowlists; route/device/account/payload drift requires reapproval; voice/mobile cannot bypass approval; unsupported Accessibility, phone, payment, booking, and automated Kakao send remain unavailable
r23_6m_phase_m3_real_route_integration.notes: Deterministic M3 certification uses fake stores/providers only and checks source guards for prohibited Android capabilities. Real external E2E is separately infrastructure-gated.

r23_6m_phase_m4_constrained_accessibilit.assertionIntent: constrained Android Accessibility execution is a fallback-only, app/action/version/device/recipient/message/approval-bound route; KakaoTalk is the initial certified adapter, WhatsApp/Instagram/Messenger remain architecture-only NOT_CERTIFIED, UI contract drift/user interruption/timeout fail closed, and arbitrary clicks/typing/coordinates remain unavailable
r23_6m_phase_m4_constrained_accessibilit.notes: No real Android app send is performed. Real E2E remains separately device/app/account gated.

r23_6m_phase_m4a_astra_guided_device_con.assertionIntent: provider-neutral DeviceUIReasoner lets Astra propose exactly one typed UI action from minimized observation while NAgex Action Gate remains the only authority for app/action/device/recipient/message/route/approval/budget/user-interruption validation; deterministic adapters stay preferred and sensitive screens/redacted observations fail closed
r23_6m_phase_m4a_astra_guided_device_con.notes: No live Astra call, no real Android send, and no direct execution authority. AstraDeviceUIReasoner is schema/gate tested with injected deterministic proposal function.

r23_6m_phase_m4b_real_astra_device_loop.assertionIntent: AstraDeviceUIReasoner has a real provider call path that sends minimized synthetic UI observation to strict structured output, parses one typed proposal, records usage, and then stops at NAgex Action Gate; deterministic known UI invokes zero Astra calls, recovery invokes Astra only as fallback, and failure modes fail closed before any device action
r23_6m_phase_m4b_real_astra_device_loop.notes: Uses fake fetch for provider-contract certification. Actual live Astra diagnostic remains environment-gated and must not be reported PASS without a real configured API key.

r23_6m_phase_m4c_real_accessibility_actu.assertionIntent: real Android accessibility actuator repair: device capability inventory exposes Android OS-derived accessibility state; KakaoTalk 26.8.2 has exact sanitized screen contracts; bounded non-send AccessibilityNodeInfo primitives are implemented; Astra recovery remains advisory/gated and send remains disabled for M4C-R1.
r23_6m_phase_m4c_real_accessibility_actu.notes: No live Android send, no screenshot streaming, no coordinate-only execution, and no arbitrary Accessibility action.

r23_6m_phase_m4c_r2a_plan_delivery_dispa.assertionIntent: server-bound ACCESSIBILITY_EXECUTE_PLAN delivery and Android dispatch wiring: heartbeat pending-command transport is reused, command envelopes carry approval-bound approvedText plus SHA-256 payload hash, Android verifies device/tenant/user/expiry/replay/accessibility/package/recipient/order before bounded AccessibilityService calls, result reporting is typed and send actions remain blocked.
r23_6m_phase_m4c_r2a_plan_delivery_dispa.notes: No live Android send, no new command channel, no raw message logging, no coordinates, no arbitrary automation, and no Astra call.

r23_6m_phase_m4c_r2b_android_auth_enroll.assertionIntent: Android device enrollment authentication UX: normal users sign in through the existing auth/login contract, the returned session id is stored in EncryptedSharedPreferences and never rendered, enrollment uses Authorization Bearer, expired auth clears the encrypted session, logout clears session state, and remote auth requires HTTPS.
r23_6m_phase_m4c_r2b_android_auth_enroll.notes: Source-level Android contract guard. No live server, no device action, no raw session ids.

r23_6m_phase_m4c_r2c_device_command_enqu.assertionIntent: governed Accessibility execute-plan enqueue API: authenticated user can enqueue only an approval-bound KakaoTalk ACCESSIBILITY_EXECUTE_PLAN for their own active enrolled device; wrong tenant/user/device, inactive device, missing/expired/mismatched approval, route/app/version drift, send/raw/arbitrary actions, duplicate active plans, and expired queued commands fail closed; heartbeat delivery consumes the pending command once.
r23_6m_phase_m4c_r2c_device_command_enqu.notes: No generic command passthrough, no raw store mutation route, no real Android action, no send.

r23_6m_d4b_gmail_canonical_email.assertionIntent: SEND_EMAIL remains distinct from SEND_MESSAGE and the real Gmail execution wrapper freezes SERVER/GOOGLE/GMAIL_API plus provider-account, recipient, content, attachment, and reply authority; successful Gmail API acceptance maps only to non-synthetic PROVIDER_ACCEPTED evidence and never delivery or read confirmation
r23_6m_d4b_gmail_canonical_email.notes: D4B automated certification uses the real GmailService, GoogleCapabilityExecutionPipeline, approval store, credential boundary, and Gmail response mapper with a deterministic provider transport. A controlled external Gmail send remains separately PENDING.

r23_7c_c_real_image_creation_runtime.notes: Validates R23.7C-C Real Image Creation Runtime: ImageExecutor, CreationProviderRouter selection, OpenAI & Google image adapters, binary image storage persistence, thin ArtifactStore projection, revision lineage across providers, tenant/user isolation, and real provider certification.

r23_7c_c_canonical_image_serving.assertionIntent: canonical image-serving HTTP contract: POST-returned imageUrl must be genuinely GET-fetchable with byte-identical content, correct MIME, and tenant/owner-isolated
r23_7c_c_canonical_image_serving.notes: Fixes the BROKEN_SUCCESS_CONTRACT root cause: no GET route ever existed for /api/v1/creations/images/:imageId, so the generic /api/v1/creations/:id handler absorbed it and 404'd against the wrong store. Certifies the new dedicated route (checked before the generic handler), reusing the same ImageStore instance and its existing tenant/owner authorization, with an explicit BinaryApiResult response variant (never base64-wrapped JSON, never a filesystem path or provider URL).

r23_7c_c_provider_neutral_preview.assertionIntent: a completed image artifact's ArtifactStore.preview never contains provider/model identity; ImageRecord.providerExecutionMetadata still carries it for technical/audit surfaces; Personal Home Recent Creations (desktop and mobile, real render) never surfaces provider identity; existing image creation/history behavior is unchanged; the new preview text is not a raw i18n key
r23_7c_c_provider_neutral_preview.notes: Fixes a confirmed TECHNICAL_UI_LEAK found while closing the desktop-history blocker: ImageExecutor's ArtifactStore.saveCompleted() previously set preview to `Image generated via ${providerId} (...)`, which flows unmodified through PersonalHomeService (summary: artifact.preview) into personal-home-view.js's rendered Recent Creations card on both desktop and mobile, in both locales, after any successful image generation. Fix changed the source to a plain, provider-neutral, locale-neutral `Image (${aspectRatio})`, matching the existing preview convention for other artifact types (e.g. "Grounded research result"). Provider/model identity remains fully available in ImageRecord.providerExecutionMetadata, never touched.

r23_7c_c_canonical_desktop_history.assertionIntent: GET /api/v1/creations and GET /api/v1/creations/:id merge ImageStore-backed real image creations into the same response shape CreationStore records already use — tenant/owner isolated, session-precedence preserved, deterministic newest-first ordering across mixed store types, no duplicate representation, variation lineage intact — and the existing #create-history-list renderer accepts the real (unmocked) canonical image URL as an actual
r23_7c_c_canonical_desktop_history.notes: Closes the sole remaining R23.7C-C closure-audit blocker: a real IMAGE creation is never written to CreationStore (it lives only in ImageStore, thinly projected into ArtifactStore for Personal Home), so GET /api/v1/creations — reading CreationStore exclusively — could never show it in the Studio's own history panel, even though that same panel just generated it. Adds imageRecordToCreationListItem() in creation.routes.ts, merging ImageStore's real record (never ArtifactStore's lossy preview, which embeds the provider id) into both the list route and the generic single-GET route (used by the history card's Open action) at the HTTP-response boundary only — no new store, no dual-write. Test I runs a minimal static+creation-routes-only server bound to a deterministic fake provider (never the real OpenAIImageAdapter createServerInstance() would wire), so this file can never reach a real provider regardless of environment.

r23_7c_c_artifact_delivery_identity.assertionIntent: shared caller-identity contract: a valid nagex_session (R13) is authoritative for POST /creations/generate and GET /creations/images/:imageId, caller-supplied X-NAgex-Tenant/X-Principal-Id headers carry no authority, and (Security Gate S1) a request with no valid session — including a malformed credential — has no identity and the route refuses
r23_7c_c_artifact_delivery_identity.notes: Fixes the browser-authentication root cause confirmed by live server evidence: a native request cannot attach custom headers, so it always resolved to the route's hardcoded default identity, which did not match the real tenant/owner of a session-authenticated user's own image. Adds src/http/request-identity.ts as the one shared identity resolver (session cookie first, header/default fallback unchanged) so creation and later retrieval agree on identity for a real logged-in user, while ImageStore.get()'s strict tenant+owner equality and its fail-closed 404 (no existence disclosure) remain completely unchanged. Does not touch the pre-existing img_93b85a5d7a103e7bdaaeff97 record from the old identity path.

security_s2a_webhook_authenticity.assertionIntent: Security Gate S2A webhook authenticity through the real entry points: a Telegram request without the server-configured secret-token header, and a Slack request without a valid v0 signature over the authentic raw body inside the replay window, is refused (401) before identity lookup, memory read, conversation write, model call, plan resolution or outbound send; a missing or unusable server secret fails closed (503) and never disables verification; the url_verification challenge is not echoed unsigned; a verified Slack delivery is processed once; secrets and message text never appear in a response or the operator log; an authentic request still flows through the unchanged pipeline.

No network, no model, no provider credentials.

security_s2a_webhook_contract.assertionIntent: Source contract that keeps the S2A boundary from regressing: both webhook routes verify before the challenge/processing, only those routes hand channel updates to the services, the verifier uses configuration secrets, constant-time comparison and the raw buffer (never a re-serialised body), a missing secret is a refusal, and the HTTP layer passes the original bytes to SIGNED_WEBHOOK routes.
security_s2a_webhook_contract.notes: Reads production source only; behavior is certified by security_s2a_webhook_authenticity.

security_s2b_channel_identity_ownership.assertionIntent: Security Gate S2B channel identity ownership through the real entry points: a client-supplied Telegram/Slack id never links (the old link routes refuse and write nothing); a link is created only when a one-time, short-lived, single-use challenge issued to a signed-in principal is redeemed from the channel itself through the S2A-authenticated webhook, bound to the issuing principal, tenant, integration and operation and to the sender/workspace taken from verified platform data; unknown, expired, replayed, wrong-integration, wrong-sender, group/non-DM, edited and malformed redemptions link nothing and write nothing; an identity already linked to another principal is never silently taken over; two simultaneous redemptions of one challenge link at most one account; a forged or secret-less webhook cannot redeem or spend a challenge; challenge codes are never logged, audited, replied or stored; the unlinked-sender policy is unchanged.
security_s2b_channel_identity_ownership.notes: Real handleAsyncApiRequest/route/service entry points with tripwires on link writes, conversation writes, memory reads, model calls and outbound sends, plus the real application wiring over a localhost HTTP server with real session cookies and signed webhooks. No network, no model, no provider credentials.

security_s2b_ownership_contract.assertionIntent: Source contract that keeps the S2B boundary from regressing: no route links or lists channel identities from client input, link attempts are handled before identity resolution/conversation/memory/model and consume+link share one synchronous step, the challenge store uses a CSPRNG and keeps only digests, identity stores never overwrite another principal's link, both channels share one challenge store, and the UI no longer asks for an external account id.
security_s2b_ownership_contract.notes: Reads production source only; behavior is certified by security_s2b_channel_identity_ownership.

security_s2c_outbound_recipient_authorit.assertionIntent: Security Gate S2C outbound recipient authority through the real entry points: a signed-in caller can send to, and notify, only itself. Telegram/Slack send derives the destination (and, for Slack, the workspace) from the caller's own ownership-proven S2B link; a body chat/channel/workspace is only an assertion that must equal it, and an arbitrary, another user's, another tenant's, unverified or missing destination is refused before the provider is invoked. notifications/dispatch makes the authenticated caller the only recipient (a differing principal or tenant is refused with zero notification write and zero channel fan-out); its channel fan-out uses only proven links; trusted internal dispatch is unchanged and unreachable over HTTP. A missing credential, provider rejection or network failure is never reported as delivered, and no bot token reaches a response, audit event or log.
security_s2c_outbound_recipient_authorit.notes: Real handleAsyncApiRequest/route/service/engine entry points and the real application wiring over a localhost HTTP server, with a recording fake provider behind the Telegram and Slack clients (nothing real is contacted) counting provider invocations, notification writes and fan-out.

security_s2c_authority_contract.assertionIntent: Source contract that keeps the S2C boundary from regressing: no route calls a channel provider, the send routes go through sendToOwnChannel with the session identity, the services decide every authority question before the provider and trust only proven links, the notification route reaches only dispatchForCaller and nothing under src/http calls the internal dispatch, and the adapters never fabricate success or log an error object.
security_s2c_authority_contract.notes: Reads production source only; behavior is certified by security_s2c_outbound_recipient_authority.

security_s2d_tenant_resource_ownership.assertionIntent: Security Gate S2D tenant resource ownership through the real entry points: the execution history is scoped to the caller's tenant AND principal (another tenant, another principal in the same tenant and the legacy demo seed are never listed; the route keeps its shape). An upload can be completed only by the caller that initiated it, on the object key the server derived: an unknown, foreign or already-completed upload and a differing/folded/traversal/foreign key are refused BEFORE any storage read, write, delete or signed-URL issue, create no capture, and never echo identifiers; a delete removes only the capture owner's own object; a record from before S2D that points at another owner's object never reaches storage; server-derived keys always sit under the caller's own prefix and a capture id is server-generated.
security_s2d_tenant_resource_ownership.notes: Real handleApiRequest/handleAsyncApiRequest entry points and a real localhost HTTP server, with tripwires counting every call to the shared application storage provider. No network, no model, no provider credentials.

security_s2d_ownership_contract.assertionIntent: Source contract that keeps the S2D boundary from regressing: completeUpload looks up the caller's own pending capture and validates the key before any storage access and never creates a capture from a client key; every storage access that follows a capture record goes through the ownership guard; no route calls storage directly; keys are bound to the record id; the execution history is filtered by tenant and principal and never returned as the shared array.
security_s2d_ownership_contract.notes: Reads production source only; behavior is certified by security_s2d_tenant_resource_ownership.

security_s2e_auth_abuse.assertionIntent: Security Gate S2E authentication abuse and the trusted client-IP boundary through the real HTTP server, with a tripwire on every scrypt call: the TCP peer is the client and X-Forwarded-For counts only through an explicitly configured trusted proxy (right-to-left, never the leftmost entry, never CF-Connecting-IP, invalid configuration or a malformed chain falls back to the peer, IPv6 bucketed by /64); rotating the forged header, the peer or the account cannot escape the per-IP, per-account and pair throttles; login, reactivate and delete-cancel share one guess budget, a throttled request performs ZERO password hashing and is uniform for existing and unknown accounts; reactivate/delete-cancel no longer reveal account state and still work for the legitimate owner; signup/forgot/resend use the same resolver and guard; throttling is progressive, capped, self-recovering and memory-bounded; audit and session addresses come from the trusted resolver; the test peer seam is refused in production and ignored by a normal server.

security_s2e_authabuse_contract.assertionIntent: Source contract that keeps the S2E boundary from regressing: no address header is read outside server_web, the resolver is peer-first/right-to-left with no Cloudflare trust or hardcoded ranges, only the HTTP layer registers an address and routes only read it, the test peer seam is a programmatic option refused in production and absent from the real start path, login/reactivate/delete-cancel/signup are throttled before any password hashing with no wrong-state oracle, forgot/resend share the guard, and the guard keeps three dimensions, a bounded store and capped progressive cooldowns.

jev_shadow_runtime.assertionIntent: JEV shadow-mode advisory contract: typed minimal output only; shadow evaluation is logged after the authoritative router decision without changing provider, task kind, fallback, approval, execution or memory authority; safe telemetry excludes prompt/answer/reasoning/secrets; the deterministic synthetic benchmark covers current TaskKinds and fails closed on invalid schema or systematic high-reasoning downgrades.
jev_shadow_runtime.notes: No network, no paid provider calls. Benchmark providers never generate; current router policy is measured offline.

nebius_nemotron_provider.assertionIntent: Nebius Token Factory / NVIDIA Nemotron provider adapter against a fake and a real local OpenAI-compatible endpoint: the configured provider uses the canonical URL, model and the server-side credential only (an unsafe base URL or a missing key leaves it UNCONFIGURED and sends nothing); success is normalized (content, usage incl. reasoning tokens, finish reason, request id); hidden provider reasoning (reasoning_content, reasoning, inline think blocks) is dropped and never returned, logged or kept; 401/403/429/5xx/network/timeout/malformed/truncated output are each reported with a fixed reason vocabulary, retried at most once for network/5xx only, and never reported as a result; no secret reaches a log, error, status or result.
nebius_nemotron_provider.notes: Fake fetch plus one local HTTP server on 127.0.0.1. The paid Nebius API is never called; the opt-in real certification is scripts/nebius-live-cert.mjs.

nebius_nemotron_routing.assertionIntent: Task-aware routing of Nemotron inside the canonical UnifiedModelRouter/ModelRoutingPolicy: PLAN, RESEARCH_SYNTHESIS and MEETING_PREP prefer NEBIUS (even over an already-live provider); every other TaskKind keeps exactly its pre-existing decision and Nemotron is not even a fallback for it; failures of the preferred provider (429, 401/403, 5xx, 404, timeout, network, malformed, validator rejection, no credential, degraded) fall back to the existing approved providers with a recorded preferredProvider/actualProvider/fallbackReason, never as a fabricated success; an explicit provider choice is never overridden; Nemotron's capability declaration is evidence-graded (nothing beyond chat completion is claimed as supported); telemetry carries task, provider, model, latency and token counts but no prompt, answer, reasoning or credential.
nebius_nemotron_routing.notes: Real providers with injected fetch; AiService methods drive the TaskKinds. No network, no paid call.

nebius_nemotron_contract.assertionIntent: Source contract that keeps the Nebius/Nemotron integration inside the canonical model architecture: the credential, URL and configuration live only in providers.ts; no route or AiService mentions the provider; feature code reaches the model only through the router; the preference table is routing data consulted only by the policy comparator and never by an explicit override; hidden reasoning is reduced to a boolean in the adapter; retry is bounded and every call has a timeout and an unsafe base URL is refused; the failure vocabulary is fixed and logs carry no provider message; the real-API certification is a separate opt-in script.
nebius_nemotron_contract.notes: Reads production source only; behavior is certified by nebius_nemotron_provider and nebius_nemotron_routing.
